why: With *for forty minutes* before a past moment, *had waited* is also correct English (Murphy 15-16). *was waiting* is rejected: a completed duration up to a past moment needs the past perfect.

*Despite the rain, ...* nearly copies the card's examples, and the open gap also takes *Before / After the rain* and *Notwithstanding*. A new sentence with a bank of card words (and the card's mistake *Despite of*) leaves one answer; the point (despite + noun) is on the B2.1 card.

fix.q: ___ her knee injury, she finished the marathon.
fix.why: *Despite* + noun (*her knee injury*); *although* and *even though* need subject + verb, and *despite* has no *of*.
fix.why_lv: *Despite* + lietvārds (*her knee injury*); aiz *although* un *even though* vajag teikuma priekšmetu un darbības vārdu, un *despite* lieto bez *of*.

why: The bracket hint is fine (word order and *to* are the point), but *so as not to* is not on the conj_clauses card and the sentence nearly copies the card example (*I wrote it down so that I wouldn't forget it*). New sentence with the card's *in order to*; the split *to not miss* is correct modern English, so it is accepted.

fix.q: I set two alarms in order ___ my early flight. (not / miss)
fix.why: Purpose, negative: *in order not to* + base form.
fix.why_lv: Nolūks noliegumā: *in order not to* + pamatforma.

why: The task is the card's own example and mistake (*Take an umbrella in case it rains / will rain*), so the answer is on the help card. New sentence; *should* after *in case* is correct (readers' *should rain*), so it is accepted; *might / could* after *in case* are not standard and *will* is the card's mistake.

fix.q: I'll leave you my number in case you ___ any problems with the flat. (have)

why: The cond_third card is taught up to B2.2, and the *if*-part second makes it more than a copy of the basic pattern; a B2.2 revision of a card point is allowed.
The card teaches *could have / might have* when the result is less sure, so both are correct here.
The bracket words must be put in order with *to*, which is the point (card mistake *She asked me don't call*); reported orders are on the rep_questions card up to B2.2.

*He apologised for being late* is the rep_verbs card's own example, so the answer is on the help card. New sentence; *for having* + 3rd form is correct and accepted; *about* is rejected (not the standard pattern, and the card teaches *apologise for*).

fix.q: She apologised ___ the meeting without a word. (leave)

why: *suggested taking a taxi* is the card's mistake example corrected (*He suggested me to take a taxi*), and the gap also takes *that we (should) take*. New sentence, with the clause answers the readers found accepted (Murphy 34 allows present, *should* and past after *suggest*).

fix.q: Our guide suggested ___ the museum early to avoid the queues. (visit)
fix.why: *suggest* + *-ing* (or *suggest that we visit / should visit*), never *suggest to*.
fix.why_lv: *suggest* + darbības vārds ar *-ing* (vai *suggest that we visit / should visit*), nekad *suggest to*.

why: With no time signal, *is going to start* and *is starting* are as correct as *starts / will start*. The level flag is moot: the task is already practice only (role learn).

Without context *was crying* (still crying) is correct too, so the task did not decide the form. A situation that shows the crying is over rules it out; *had cried* is also correct and accepted. *cried* stays wrong (the state follows an earlier action).

fix.q: She was smiling when I saw her, but her eyes were red because she ___ . (cry)
fix.why: The crying was over before that moment and we see its result: *had been* + *-ing* (*had cried* is also possible).
fix.why_lv: Raudāšana bija beigusies pirms tā brīža, un mēs redzam tās rezultātu: *had been* + *-ing* (iespējams arī *had cried*).

why: The sentence is the cond_mixed card's mistake example (*If he had studied medicine, he would be a doctor now*), and *might / could be* were not accepted. New sentence; *might not* and the continuous are accepted.

fix.q: If I had learned to drive at eighteen, I ___ so much on taxis now. (not / spend)
fix.why: A past event with a result now: *would* + base form, because of *now*.
fix.why_lv: Pagātnes notikums ar sekām tagad: *would* + pamatforma, jo ir *now*.

why: Nearly a copy of the card example *If I weren't so shy, I would have asked her*, and *hadn't been* (shy at the party) is also correct, as both readers wrote. New sentence with a lasting fact; both answers are accepted, and the explanation says why.

fix.q: If I ___ allergic to cats, I would have stayed at Anna's place last weekend. (not / be)
fix.why: A lasting fact now (*allergic*) with a result in the past: *if* + past (*weren't*). *hadn't been* is also correct if you think only of last weekend.
fix.why_lv: Pastāvīgs fakts tagad (*allergic*) ar sekām pagātnē: *if* + pagātne (*weren't*). Pareizi arī *hadn't been*, ja domā tikai par pagājušo nedēļas nogali.

why: Any result linker is correct after the semicolon; the readers' formal ones are added. *so ,* is rejected (*so* after a semicolon takes no comma and is not a formal linker).

*accepted* would give *If she accepted the job, she would be living there now*, which makes no sense (accepting now cannot mean living there now); only the past perfect fits. The mixed conditional is on the B2.2 card.

*I wish I had more time* is the cond_advanced card's mistake example corrected, so the answer is on the help card; *could have* was also correct. New sentence; *could live* and the continuous are accepted. *wish* + past is on the B2.2 card, so the level stays.

fix.q: I wish I ___ closer to my office; the commute takes hours. (live)
fix.why: A wish about now: *wish* + past (*could live* is also correct).
fix.why_lv: Vēlēšanās par tagadni: *wish* + pagātne (pareizi arī *could live*).

why: The contraction *'s* (*the speaker's late*) must be listed. Level: *unless* is on the B2.2 cond_advanced card (with its mistake *unless it doesn't*), so it stays.
The readers' point (easy) is not a fault, but the sentence repeats the card example's frame (*Had I known about the delay, I would have taken a taxi*). New sentence with another verb, same point.

fix.q: ___ we left ten minutes earlier, we would have caught the ferry. (have)
fix.why: Formal, without *if*: *Had we left* = *If we had left*.
fix.why_lv: Formāli, bez *if*: *Had we left* = *If we had left*.

why: *It's high time the government was doing something* is correct (past continuous after *it's time*). *should do* and *does* are rejected: not standard after *it's high time*.

*hadn't used* (a complaint about something already done) is also correct, but past perfect after *would rather* is not on the card. *In future* makes the wish about from now on, so only *didn't use* fits; *wouldn't use* is not standard.

fix.q: In future, I'd rather you ___ my phone without asking. (not / use)
fix.why: *I'd rather* + another person + past: what I want someone else not to do. *In future* shows it is about from now on.
fix.why_lv: *I'd rather* + cita persona + pagātne: ko es gribu, lai cits nedara. *In future* rāda, ka runa ir par turpmāko laiku.

why: *She insisted on paying* is the card's own mistake example corrected, and the gap also takes *that she (should) pay*. New sentence with the clause answers accepted (the card teaches *insist* + *that* too).

fix.q: My father insisted ___ us to the airport. (drive)
fix.why: *insist on* + *-ing* (or *insist that he drive / should drive*).
fix.why_lv: *insist on* + darbības vārds ar *-ing* (vai *insist that he drive / should drive*).

why: Clause answers (*where we should / could go*) are correct English after *decide where*. Level: question word + *to* is on the B2.2 ind_advanced card, so it stays.

*If it weren't / wasn't for your advice, I would never have applied* is correct and common (present support, past result, as in the mixed conditional). Reader 1's point (fixed phrase) is not a fault: the card teaches it.
*deny* also takes a *that*-clause, as the card's *watch* says for *admit*; the readers' clause answers are correct.
*of having sold* is correct (the earlier action stressed). The preposition is the point of the task (card mistake *accused him for*).
*Anyone who / Anybody who / The person who / Everyone who* contain the bracket word and are correct English. The hint *(who)* stays: the learner forms *Whoever* from it.
*if* after a preposition is rejected (nonstandard; the card says *whether*). But the sentence is the card's own example (*It depends on whether the budget is approved*), so it is replaced.

fix.q: Our holiday plans depend on ___ my boss gives me the week off.

why: *should go* after *It's about time* is not standard English; only the past is correct. After 032 and 034 are changed, the frames no longer repeat.
No problem found; reader 2 marked it fine.
*It's about time you called your mother* is the card's example sentence, so the answer is on the help card, and it repeats 030's *about time you*. New sentence, same options pattern.

fix.q: Choose the correct option: It's about time the landlord ___ the heating.
fix.why: *It's (high / about) time* + subject + past: it should happen now, and it is already late.
fix.why_lv: *It's* (*high / about*) *time* + teikuma priekšmets + pagātne: tam jau vajadzētu notikt, un ir jau vēlu.

why: *It's high time we went* is the card's mistake example corrected (and its *It's high time we left*). New sentence; the bank still has real forms that do not fit (*have booked, will book, had booked*).

fix.q: It's high time we ___ the tickets. The concert is next week.
fix.why: *It's (high / about) time* + subject + past: it should happen now, and it is already late.
fix.why_lv: *It's* (*high / about*) *time* + teikuma priekšmets + pagātne: tam jau vajadzētu notikt, un ir jau vēlu.

why: A clone of 020's frame (*It's high time the government / the city ___ something about ...* → *did*). New sentence with another verb.

fix.q: Choose the correct option: It's high time the city ___ more cycle lanes.
fix.why: *It's (high / about) time* + subject + past: it should happen now, and it is already late.
fix.why_lv: *It's* (*high / about*) *time* + teikuma priekšmets + pagātne: tam jau vajadzētu notikt, un ir jau vēlu.

why: *began*, *that you started*, *were looking*, *started job-hunting* and *for you to start* are correct and keep the meaning. Rejected: *should start* (not standard after *it's high time*), *found a new job* (changes the meaning), *to start* without *you* and *I started* (drop or change the person). The start is the task, so the prompt stays.
accept: It's high time you began looking for a new job.
It is high time you began looking for a new job.
It's high time that you started looking for a new job.
It is high time that you started looking for a new job.
It's high time you were looking for a new job.
It is high time you were looking for a new job.
It's high time you started job-hunting.
It is high time you started job-hunting.
It's high time for you to start looking for a new job.
It is high time for you to start looking for a new job.

why: Level stays (*would sooner* is on the B2.2 card), but the sentence is the card's example (*I'd sooner take the train than drive*). New sentence with the same kind of bank.

fix.q: I'd sooner ___ a sandwich at my desk than go to that noisy canteen.
fix.why: *I'd rather / I'd sooner* + base form: what I prefer to do myself.
fix.why_lv: *I'd rather / I'd sooner* + pamatforma: ko es pats labāk darītu.

why: Reader 2 marked it fine; no problem found.

The mistake is a real one, but it is the card's own mistake example (*I'd rather to walk*), *I'd rather you came a bit earlier* is a card example too, and *I'd sooner stay here than go out* copies the wrong sentence's pattern. New wrong sentence and right sentences about three different things.

fix.correct: I'd rather to cook at home than eat out.
wrong: I'd rather you didn't tell Mark yet.
It's high time they fixed the road.
We'd sooner leave early on Friday.
fix.why: *I'd rather* + base form, without *to*: *I'd rather cook*.

why: The start is the task (rewrite), so the near-copy is intended. The readers' paraphrases are correct and keep the meaning; *wouldn't bring* is rejected (not standard after *I'd rather you*).
accept: I'd rather you didn't bring your dog into the office.
I would rather you didn't bring your dog into the office.
I'd rather you didn't bring your dog to work.
I would rather you didn't bring your dog to work.
